mine.title: An agent judged the game replay for you
mine.said: Game Week Bites' check said you would step through a replayed game. At your go-with-the-recommended word, an agent judged it instead, and it passed. That was Claude's call.
options: Wait for you to step through it
mine.why: The bar names you as the judge, but you said these weren't blocked on you.
mine.undo: Reopen the check and step through the replay yourself.

mine.title: Your taps wait their turn too
mine.said: Claude chose, alone, to pace every request the phone sends home, yours included, so after a burst a tap can wait up to two seconds.
mine.why: Leaving your taps unpaced gives up the bound on how hard the phone can push home.
mine.undo: Let your own requests skip the pace, and narrow the promise to background sends.

mine.title: How the phone retries when you're away
mine.said: Away from home, the phone now tries every thirty seconds, doubling to ten minutes, while your own taps still go at once. Claude's call, under your standing word to take the recommended.
options: A fixed five-minute wait for everything
mine.why: The phone can't tell being away from home being down, so the wait decides how soon things go once you're back.
mine.undo: Change the hold times, or hold your taps too.

mine.title: A SQLite advisory set aside until February
mine.said: Claude set aside a security advisory on the SQLite the server bundles, dated to be looked at again by February eleventh, because no fixed version can be reached yet.
options: A dated ignore, backed by a written rule
mine.why: The flaw needs a database file someone else wrote, and the server only opens its own. No convention says whether that is enough.
mine.undo: Drop the ignore once a library release reaches the fixed SQLite, then upgrade.

mine.title: Drafts show a red check
mine.said: Claude made draft pull requests run no checks, and show a red gate until they're marked ready.
options: Drafts run nothing and fail the gate
mine.why: A skipped gate would count as passed, so a draft could look green without being checked.
mine.undo: Drop the draft conditions from the three workflows.

mine.title: Every new video's colours shift a little
mine.said: Claude changed how videos are converted to colour, so every new render, Build Journal shorts included, looks slightly different from before. Old videos are untouched.
options: The new colour standard for every video
mine.why: You'd notice it in a re-render, but no check settles which is right.
mine.undo: Revert the conversion in the renderer's plan.

mine.title: Two caps stay off Settings
mine.said: Claude left Soundbites' six and Studio's take budget off the Settings limits, since each already shows its count beside the recorder.
options: Shown on their own screens only
A row in Settings as well
mine.why: The settings story asks for every cap there, but these two are read where the next take is decided.
mine.undo: Add the two rows to Settings' limits.

mine.title: Home makes clips' frames itself
mine.said: Home now draws walk-through clips' frames itself, and frames taken in a session aren't kept. Claude's call, which you agreed to on the eleventh.
options: Carry frames through the mailbox's brief
A new mailbox folder for frames
mine.why: The mailbox refuses images by design, and a new folder needs your amendment.
mine.undo: Build the route that carries frames through the mailbox.

asks.question: Should every GitHub Action the workflows use be pinned to a commit, rather than a version tag?
asks.said: The workflows could pin every action they use to an exact commit, which is safer and takes more upkeep, or keep version tags with a written reason.
asks.whyYours: It trades a supply-chain risk against how much upkeep the workflows take, and the repos are yours to keep.

options.says: Pin every action to a commit; Dependabot moves the pins
options.unblocks: U8 opens with every unpinned finding cleared

options.says: Keep version tags, and record why in zizmor's config
options.unblocks: U8 opens with the finding set aside, and a reason
